result: UNSUCCESSFUL. No interpretable serial zebrafish section obtained
scientific_limit: Mechanics of agarose-paraffin interface are inferred from observed separation, not proved experimentally. No tissue micrograph, measured modulus, or successful repeat invented.
human_review: NOT APPROVED. Compare full-size source photographs and listen to film before replacing any original.

chapters.title: Small specimens and a question
chapters.speech: I needed histological sections of zebrafish embryos. They were small, and their orientation mattered: a slice through the wrong plane could miss the anatomy I wanted to study.
chapters.source: Owner's 2025 image of five oriented zebrafish specimens, no outcome claimed.

chapters.title: An orientation scaffold
chapters.speech: My first step used two percent agarose as a support. I could position the specimens before the paraffin step, with the hope of preserving the chosen plane during sectioning.
chapters.source: Owner first-person account, 2% agarose preparation; placement photograph.

chapters.title: Two materials in sequence
chapters.speech: The proposal depended on two different materials. Agarose maintained orientation; paraffin was supposed to support thin sections after processing. The second stage would have to integrate with the first.
chapters.source: First-person description, not a claim of chemical bonding between matrices.

chapters.title: The laboratory attempt
chapters.speech: This is the real processing apparatus from that attempt. It records what was tried, but a photograph of the instrument is not evidence that a usable section was made.
chapters.source: Owner late-2025 photograph of laboratory histological processing instrument.

chapters.title: Where the interface mattered
chapters.speech: Instead of behaving like one mechanically coherent block, the embedded materials formed distinguishable layers. A sectioning method that works with one solid block may fail when the material interface separates.
chapters.source: Observed layer separation in first-person record; hypothetical mechanical explanation labelled.

chapters.title: At the microtome
chapters.speech: Here is the actual block in the microtome. At sectioning the material separated and broke apart. The problem was no longer merely positioning a fish; it was obtaining a sectionable composite.
chapters.source: Owner microtomy-failure photograph: actual preparation, no successful tissue section.

chapters.title: No interpretable section
chapters.speech: I did not obtain reliable, interpretable histological sections from this sequence. Nothing here is a successful stained slide, and these photographs should not be used to imply one.
chapters.source: Failed result in first-person field note. No fabricated microscopy or quantitative output.

chapters.title: The next trial would differ
chapters.speech: The failure suggests questions for a new method: embedding compatibility, processing, and orientation controls. Those are experiments still to perform, not results I have already produced.
chapters.source: Future method hypotheses only; exact procedure for successful follow-up not established.
